newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish trawler nets drink.
newsitem.headline: Irish trawler nets drink.

text.p: The crew of a Northern Irish trawler caught an unexpected Christmas present in its nets this year - bottles and bottles of whiskey.
"On the 15th of December we were fishing off Whitehaven and hauling the nets aboard for the last haul of the day," crewman Arnold Smith told Irish radio.
"It was bottles and bottles of whiskey and wine....we were quite pleased at the time as it was getting close to Christmas."
The catch apparently came from a container packed with an estimated 120,000 bottles of alcohol which was washed overboard from another vessel 18 months ago.
Smith said the catch was immediately tested to make sure its submersion had not damaged the contents.
"It was well tested before we got home. It was good stuff," said Smith, whose vessel, the Christian Borum, fishes for cod out of Ardglass on Northern Ireland's eastern coast.
He said that other boats had started to retrieve alcohol from the sea bed but that he planned to keep the location of the catch secret.
"I'd say there will be a few people out there trying to get a bottle or two. We are just keeping it to ourselves for the time being."
